title: 2015 年全国硕士研究生招生考试 英语（二）

sections.title: Section I　完形填空
sections.dir: Read the following text. Choose the best word(s) for each numbered blank and mark A, B, C or D on the ANSWER SHEET. (10 points)
sections.note: 主线：宁盯手机也不与陌生人搭话，实验证明开口并不尴尬。3 题 plugged into 是搭配题。

paras.en: In our contemporary culture, the prospect of communicating with — or even looking at — a stranger is virtually unbearable. Everyone around us seems to agree by the way they cling to their phones, even without a 1 on a subway.
paras.zh: 在当代文化中，与陌生人交谈——甚至只是看陌生人一眼——几乎是难以忍受的。我们身边的每个人似乎都认同这一点，从他们紧抓手机的样子就能看出来，哪怕地铁里根本没有 1。

paras.en: It's a sad reality — our desire to avoid interacting with other human beings — because there's 2 to be gained from talking to the stranger standing by you. But you wouldn't know it, 3 into your phone. This universal protection sends the 4 : "Please don't approach me."
paras.zh: 这是一个令人遗憾的现实——我们不愿与他人交往——因为与站在身边的陌生人交谈其实能收获 2。但你不会知道这一点，因为你整个人 3 在手机里。这种普遍的自我保护发出的 4 是：“请别靠近我。”

paras.en: What is it that makes us feel we need to hide 5 our screens?
paras.zh: 究竟是什么让我们觉得必须躲在屏幕 5？

paras.en: One answer is fear, according to Jon Wortmann, an executive mental coach. We fear rejection, or that our innocent social advances will be 6 as "weird." We fear we'll be 7 . We fear we'll be disruptive.
paras.zh: 高管心理教练乔恩·沃特曼认为，答案之一是恐惧。我们害怕被拒绝，害怕自己善意的社交举动会被 6 为“古怪”。我们害怕自己会 7。我们害怕自己会打扰别人。

paras.en: Strangers are inherently 8 to us, so we are more likely to feel 9 when communicating with them compared with our friends and acquaintances. To avoid this uneasiness, we 10 to our phones. "Phones become our security blanket," Wortmann says. "They are our happy glasses that protect us from what we perceive is going to be more 11 ."
paras.zh: 陌生人对我们而言天然就是 8 的，因此与朋友和熟人相比，我们同他们交流时更容易感到 9。为了回避这种不安，我们 10 手机。“手机成了我们的安全毯，”沃特曼说，“它是我们的快乐眼镜，保护我们免受我们自以为会更加 11 的东西的伤害。”

paras.en: But once we rip off the band-aid, tuck our smartphones in our pockets and look up, it doesn't 12 so bad. In one 2011 experiment, behavioral scientists Nicholas Epley and Juliana Schroeder asked commuters to do the unthinkable: Start a 13 . They had Chicago train commuters talk to their fellow 14 . "When Dr. Epley and Ms. Schroeder asked other people in the same train station to 15 how they would feel after talking to a stranger, the commuters thought their 16 would be more pleasant if they sat on their own," The New York Times summarizes. Though the participants didn't expect a positive experience, after they 17 with the experiment, "not a single person reported having been embarrassed."
paras.zh: 但一旦我们撕掉创可贴，把智能手机塞进口袋，抬起头来，情况并没有 12 得那么糟。在 2011 年的一项实验中，行为科学家尼古拉斯·埃普利和朱莉安娜·施罗德请通勤者做一件不可思议的事：发起一次 13。他们让芝加哥的火车通勤者与同车的 14 交谈。《纽约时报》总结道：“当埃普利博士和施罗德女士请同一车站的其他人 15 他们与陌生人交谈后会有什么感受时，这些通勤者认为，如果自己一个人坐着，他们的 16 会更愉快。”尽管参与者并不期待愉快的经历，但在他们 17 这项实验之后，“没有一个人报告说自己感到尴尬”。

paras.en: 18 , these commutes were reportedly more enjoyable compared with those without communication, which makes absolute sense, 19 human beings thrive off of social connections. It's that 20 : Talking to strangers can make you feel connected.
paras.zh: 18，据报道，这些通勤比没有交流的通勤更令人愉快，这完全说得通，19 人类正是靠着社会联系才得以蓬勃发展。道理就这么 20：与陌生人交谈能让你感到与他人相连。

items.exp: 定位首段末句 even without a 1 on a subway：地铁里“没有信号”正是人们只能紧抓手机的处境，signal 与上句 cling to their phones 一体呼应。permit（许可）、ticket（车票）虽能与 on a subway 搭配，但“没车票”与玩手机无关；record 更无法表达“地下无信号”。
定位第二段 because there's 2 to be gained from talking to the stranger：破折号前说“回避交流是个可悲的现实”，原因只能是“与陌生人交谈能收获很多”，故 much。B 的 little 会让“可悲”失去理由，与逻辑相反；nothing 过于绝对；another 需要前文已有“第一个”，此处没有。
定位同段 But you wouldn't know it, 3 into your phone：分词短语作状语，写人“插进、埋进”手机里，plug into 本指接电源，与上文 cling to their phones 一脉相承。beaten into（被强行灌输）、guided into、brought into 都不能与“手机”组成“沉浸其中”之意，且与主语 you 的自主性冲突。
定位 This universal protection sends the 4: "Please don't approach me."：冒号后是要传达的话语，send a message 为固定搭配，message 可指“（用行为）传达出的信息”。code（密码）、sign（迹象）、notice（通知）都不能直接带出这句“潜台词”，语义上也无法与 sends 搭配。
定位第三段 we need to hide 5 our screens：躲在屏幕后面，是“以屏幕为遮挡”，behind 表“在……背后”，与 hide 的“藏身”义最契合。under 强调被覆盖其下，beyond 指“超出”，from 表来源或分离，都无法构成“藏身于屏幕之后”的画面。
定位第四段 our innocent social advances will be 6 as "weird"：善意之举被别人“理解成”古怪，misinterpret sth as 意为“把……误解为”，故 B。misapplied（误用）、misadjusted（误调）、mismatched（搭配不当）都无法接 as “weird”，也读不出“被他人解读”这一层。
定位紧接的 We fear we'll be 7. We fear we'll be disruptive：与“打扰别人”并列的应是“被人评判”，be judged 与上句 fear rejection 同属社交恐惧。fired（被解雇）、replaced（被取代）、delayed（被耽搁）都是职场事务性遭遇，与陌生人搭话的场景错位。
定位第五段 Strangers are inherently 8 to us：陌生人本就“不熟悉”，下句 compared with our friends and acquaintances 正是这组对照。unreasonable（不讲理）、ungrateful（不知感恩）、unconventional（不合常规）都是对陌生人的价值评判，无法解释“因此更易感到不安”的因果。
定位 so we are more likely to feel 9 when communicating with them：上文连说三层 fear，下文 To avoid this uneasiness 直接点破这种感受就是“不安”，anxious 最贴。comfortable、confident 与 uneasiness 相反；angry 是愤怒，解释不了“回避”这一反应。
定位 To avoid this uneasiness, we 10 to our phones：turn to 意为“转向、求助于”，与下句 Phones become our security blanket 完全接得上。attend to 是“处理、照料”，take to 是“开始喜欢”，point to 是“指向”，三者都无法表达“把手机当依靠”。
定位 protect us from what we perceive is going to be more 11：手机被当作护身符，挡住我们“以为”会更危险的东西，protect...from 也要求填负面威胁，故 dangerous。mysterious、boring 不构成需要防护的威胁；violent 过于具体，把“陌生”窄化成“暴力”。
定位第六段 it doesn't 12 so bad：撕掉创可贴、抬起头之后，情况“并没有那么难受”，hurt 作不及物动词表“感到痛苦”，与 so bad 搭配自然。bend、decay 讲形变与腐坏，resist 表抵抗，都不能描述人的感受，也无法与 bad 连用。
定位 Start a 13：冒号后就是 talk to their fellow passengers，说明要发起的是“交谈”，start a conversation 为固定搭配。lecture（讲座）、debate（辩论）、negotiation（谈判）都带正式或对立色彩，与陌生人闲聊的语境不符。
定位 They had Chicago train commuters talk to their fellow 14：火车上的同行者就是“乘客”，passengers 与 commuters 同义呼应。trainees（受训者）、employees（雇员）、researchers（研究者）都把场景换到了培训、公司或实验室，与 train 不符。

定位 asked other people in the same train station to 15 how they would feel after talking to a stranger：问的是“事先预判”感受，故 predict；下句 the commuters thought... 正是他们预判的内容。reveal（透露）指向已经发生的事，choose、design 都无法接 how they would feel。
定位 the commuters thought their 16 would be more pleasant if they sat on their own：指这一段“乘车行程”，ride 可指搭乘交通工具的过程，与 train commuters 对应。voyage 指航海，flight 指飞行，walk 指步行，都与火车通勤不符。
定位 after they 17 with the experiment：表示“把实验做完、经历完”，go through with 意为“把……进行到底”。did away with（废除）、caught up with（赶上）、put up with（忍受）填入后，或与“实验”搭配不当，或把“完成实验”读成“取消实验”。
定位末段 18, these commutes were reportedly more enjoyable：上文说参与者原本不看好，此处给出与实际预期相反的结果，In fact 表“事实上”的转折递进。In turn 表依次、In particular 表举例、In consequence 表结果，都读不出“预期落空”的语气。
定位 which makes absolute sense, 19 human beings thrive off of social connections：后半句解释“为什么说得通”，是原因状语从句，since 表“因为”。unless 表条件、whereas 表对比、if 表假设，都无法引出这句解释。
定位末句 It's that 20: Talking to strangers can make you feel connected：冒号后是对全文的朴素概括，作者以“道理就这么简单”收束，simple 最合。funny（奇怪的）、rare（罕见的）带评价色彩却与“人人都能试”相悖；logical 侧重推理严密，不如 simple 贴合口语语气。

sections.title: Text 1　家里的压力为何更大
sections.dir: Read the following four texts. Answer the questions below each text by choosing A, B, C or D. Mark your answers on the ANSWER SHEET. (40 points)
sections.note: 主线：新研究推翻常识——家比职场更耗人。21 题要看 contrary to most surveys 的方向。

paras.en: A new study suggests that contrary to most surveys, people are actually more stressed at home than at work. Researchers measured people's cortisol, which is a stress marker, while they were at work and while they were at home and found it higher at what is supposed to be a place of refuge.
paras.zh: 一项新研究显示，与大多数调查的结论相反，人们在家其实比上班时压力更大。研究人员测量了受试者上班时和在家时的皮质醇（一种压力标志物），结果发现，在本该是避风港的家里，皮质醇水平反而更高。

paras.en: "Further contradicting conventional wisdom, we found that women as well as men have lower levels of stress at work than at home," writes one of the researchers, Sarah Damaske. In fact women even say they feel better at work, she notes. "It is men, not women, who report being happier at home than at work." Another surprise is that the findings hold true for both those with children and without, but more so for nonparents. This is why people who work outside the home have better health.
paras.zh: “进一步与常理相悖的是，我们发现，女性和男性一样，在上班时的压力水平都低于在家时，”研究者之一莎拉·达马斯克写道。她指出，女性甚至说自己上班时感觉更好。“声称在家比上班更快乐的是男性，而不是女性。”另一个意外之处是，这一结论对有孩子和没孩子的人都成立，但在无子女者身上更为明显。这也解释了为什么外出工作的人身体更健康。

paras.en: What the study doesn't measure is whether people are still doing work when they're at home, whether it is household work or work brought home from the office. For many men, the end of the workday is a time to kick back. For women who stay home, they never get to leave the office. And for women who work outside the home, they often are playing catch-up-with-household tasks. With the blurring of roles, and the fact that the home front lags well behind the workplace in making adjustments for working women, it's not surprising that women are more stressed at home.
paras.zh: 这项研究没有测量的是，人们在家时是否仍在干活——不论是家务，还是从办公室带回家的工作。对许多男性来说，一天工作结束就是放松的时候。对留在家里的女性来说，她们永远下不了班。而对在外工作的女性来说，她们常常在追赶落下的家务。角色变得模糊，加上家庭这一边在适应职场女性方面远远落后于职场，女性在家压力更大也就不奇怪了。

paras.en: But it's not just a gender thing. At work, people pretty much know what they're supposed to be doing: working, making money, doing the tasks they have to do in order to draw an income. The bargain is very pure: Employee puts in hours of physical or mental labor and employee draws out life-sustaining moola.
paras.zh: 但这不仅仅是性别问题。在职场，人们基本清楚自己该干什么：工作、挣钱、完成那些为了领取收入而必须完成的任务。这笔交易非常纯粹：雇员投入若干小时的体力或脑力劳动，然后取出维持生计的钞票。

paras.en: On the home front, however, people have no such clarity. Rare is the household in which the division of labor is so clinically and methodically laid out. There are a lot of tasks to be done, there are inadequate rewards for most of them. Your home colleagues — your family — have no clear rewards for their labor; they need to be talked into it, or if they're teenagers, threatened with complete removal of all electronic devices. Plus, they're your family. You cannot fire your family. You never really get to go home from home.
paras.zh: 然而在家庭这一边，人们没有这样的清晰感。很少有家庭能把分工安排得那么冷静精确、井然有序。要做的事情很多，其中大多数又得不到足够的回报。你的“家庭同事”——你的家人——付出劳动并没有明确的报酬；你得说服他们去做，如果他们是青少年，还得威胁没收全部电子设备。何况他们是你的家人，你没法解雇家人。你也永远无法真正从家里“下班回家”。

paras.en: So it's not surprising that people are more stressed at home. Not only are the tasks apparently infinite, the co-workers are much harder to motivate.
paras.zh: 所以，人们在家压力更大并不奇怪。不仅任务显然无穷无尽，这里的“同事”也难调动得多。

items.stem: According to Paragraph 1, most previous surveys found that home
opts: offered greater relaxation than the workplace
was an ideal place for stress measurement
generated more stress than the workplace
was an unrealistic place for relaxation
items.exp: 定位首段首句 contrary to most surveys, people are actually more stressed at home than at work：与“多数调查”相反，说明旧调查认为家比职场轻松、更能放松，故 A。C 恰是新研究的结论，被 contrary to 直接推翻，是最强干扰；D 把“家应是避风港”偷换成“家不现实”，文中没有这一评价。

items.stem: According to Damaske, who are likely to be the happiest at home?
items.exp: 定位第二段④句 It is men, not women, who report being happier at home than at work，再结合⑤句 the findings hold true for both those with children and without, but more so for nonparents：在家最快乐的是没有孩子的男性，即 childless husbands。C 多出“有孩子”这一削弱条件，A、D 都是女性，与原文相反。

items.stem: The blurring of working women's roles refers to the fact that
opts: their home is also a place for kicking back
they are both bread winners and housewives
there is often much housework left behind
it is difficult for them to leave their office
items.exp: 定位第三段末句 With the blurring of roles：上文说在外工作的女性常 playing catch-up-with-household tasks，而留在家里的女性 never get to leave the office，可见“角色模糊”指挣钱者与家务承担者两种身份重叠，故 B。A 说的是男性 kick back；C、D 各只说了一个侧面，没有点出“双重身份”。

items.stem: The word "moola" (Line 4, Para. 4) most probably means
items.exp: 定位第四段末句 Employee puts in hours of physical or mental labor and employee draws out life-sustaining moola：与“投入劳动”相对的是“取出”维持生计的东西，即工资收入，故 earnings。D 是由 life-sustaining 引发的字面联想；skills 与 energy 属于投入的一方，方向相反。

items.stem: The home front differs from the workplace in that
opts: family labor is often adequately rewarded
home is hardly a cozier working environment
household tasks are generally more motivating
division of labor at home is seldom clear-cut
items.exp: 定位第五段②句 Rare is the household in which the division of labor is so clinically and methodically laid out：家里极少有职场那样清楚的分工，故 D。A 与 inadequate rewards 相反；C 与 co-workers are much harder to motivate 相反；B 只是“家里不那么舒适”的含糊改写，未触及分工这一核心差异。

sections.title: Text 2　第一代大学生的隐形鸿沟
sections.dir: Read the following four texts. Answer the questions below each text by choosing A, B, C or D. Mark your answers on the ANSWER SHEET. (40 points)
sections.note: 主线：扩招第一代大学生却看着他们掉队，症结在实用知识而非潜力。27 题 costless 是偷换。

paras.en: For years, studies have found that first-generation college students - those who do not have a parent with a college degree — lag other students on a range of education achievement factors. Their grades are lower and their dropout rates are higher. But since such students are most likely to advance economically if they succeed in higher education, colleges and universities have pushed for decades to recruit more of them. This has created "a paradox" in that recruiting first-generation students, but then watching many of them fail, means that higher education has "continued to reproduce and widen, rather than close" an achievement gap based on social class, according to the depressing beginning of a paper forthcoming in the journal Psychological Science.
paras.zh: 多年来，研究一直发现，第一代大学生——即父母一方没有大学学历的学生——在一系列教育成就指标上都落后于其他学生。他们的成绩更低，辍学率更高。但既然这类学生一旦在高等教育中取得成功，就最有可能在经济上向上流动，高校几十年来一直在扩招他们。这就造成了“一个悖论”：据一篇即将刊于《心理科学》杂志的论文（其开篇令人沮丧）所述，招收第一代大学生、随后却眼看着他们中许多人失败，意味着高等教育“持续复制并扩大、而非缩小”了基于社会阶层的成就差距。

paras.en: But the article is actually quite optimistic, as it outlines a potential solution to this problem, suggesting that an approach (which involves a one-hour, next-to-no-cost program) can close 63 percent of the achievement gap (measured by such factors as grades) between first-generation and other students.
paras.zh: 但这篇文章其实相当乐观，因为它勾勒出了这一问题的可能解法，提出一种方法（一个仅需一小时、几乎零成本的项目）就能缩小第一代大学生与其他学生之间 63% 的成就差距（以成绩等指标衡量）。

paras.en: The authors of the paper are from different universities, and their findings are based on a study involving 147 students (who completed the project) at an unnamed private university. First generation was defined as not having a parent with a four-year college degree. Most of the first-generation students (59.1 percent) were recipients of Pell Grants, a federal grant for undergraduates with financial need, while this was true only for 8.6 percent of the students with at least one parent with a four-year degree.
paras.zh: 论文作者来自不同高校，其结论基于一项涉及某所匿名私立大学 147 名学生（完成该项目者）的研究。第一代大学生被界定为父母一方没有四年制大学学历者。多数第一代大学生（59.1%）是佩尔助学金的获得者，这是一项面向有经济困难的本科生的联邦助学金；而在父母至少一方有四年制学历的学生中，这一比例仅为 8.6%。

paras.en: Their thesis — that a relatively modest intervention could have a big impact — was based on the view that first-generation students may be most lacking not in potential but in practical knowledge about how to deal with the issues that face most college students. They cite past research by several authors to show that this is the gap that must be narrowed to close the achievement gap.
paras.zh: 他们的论点是：一项相对温和的干预也能产生很大影响。这一论点基于这样一种看法：第一代大学生最缺的也许不是潜力，而是关于如何应对多数大学生都会遇到的问题的实用知识。他们援引几位学者以往的研究，说明必须缩小这一差距，才能缩小成就差距。

paras.en: Many first-generation students "struggle to navigate the middle-class culture of higher education, learn the 'rules of the game,' and take advantage of college resources," they write. And this becomes more of a problem when colleges don't talk about the class advantages and disadvantages of different groups of students.
paras.zh: 他们写道，许多第一代大学生“艰难地应付高等教育的中产阶级文化，学习‘游戏规则’，并利用大学资源”。而当高校不谈不同学生群体的阶层优势与劣势时，这就更成问题。

paras.en: "Because US colleges and universities seldom acknowledge how social class can affect students' educational experiences, many first-generation students lack insight about why they are struggling and do not understand how students 'like them' can improve."
paras.zh: “由于美国高校很少承认社会阶层会如何影响学生的教育经历，许多第一代大学生不清楚自己为何挣扎，也不明白‘像他们这样的’学生怎样才能进步。”

items.stem: Recruiting more first-generation students has
items.exp: 定位首段④句 This has created "a paradox"：高校扩招本为帮他们向上流动，结果却看着许多人失败，反而“复制并扩大”了成就差距，即招生初衷落空，故 C。B 与 widened 相反；A 与 dropout rates are higher 相反；D 把“论文开头令人沮丧”曲解成“学生抑郁”。

items.stem: The authors of the research article are optimistic because
items.exp: 定位第二段首句 the article is actually quite optimistic, as it outlines a potential solution to this problem：乐观的根据是“问题有解”，故 C。D 用 next-to-no-cost 设套，但“几乎零成本”不等于 costless，且这只是方案特点，不是乐观的理由；A、B 文中均无依据。

items.stem: The study suggests that most first-generation students
opts: are in need of financial support
items.exp: 定位第三段③句 Most of the first-generation students (59.1 percent) were recipients of Pell Grants, a federal grant for undergraduates with financial need：多数人靠助学金，说明需要经济支持，故 C。A 把“父母一方无本科学历”误读为单亲；B、D 把“某所匿名私立大学”和“许多人失败”扩大到“多数学生”。

items.stem: The authors of the paper believe that first-generation students
opts: may lack opportunities to apply for research projects
are inexperienced in handling their issues at college
can have a potential influence on other students
are actually indifferent to the achievement gap
items.exp: 定位第四段①句 first-generation students may be most lacking not in potential but in practical knowledge about how to deal with the issues：缺的是“处理问题的实用知识”，即缺乏应对经验，故 B。A 把 practical knowledge 窄化为“申请研究项目的机会”；C、D 与“缺应对能力”这一判断无关。

items.stem: We may infer from the last paragraph that
opts: universities often reject the culture of the middle-class
students are usually to blame for their lack of resources
social class greatly helps enrich educational experiences
colleges are partly responsible for the problem in question
items.exp: 定位末段：US colleges and universities seldom acknowledge how social class can affect students' educational experiences，导致学生不明白自己为何挣扎，可见校方对问题负有一部分责任，故 D。A 把“回避谈阶层”说成“拒绝中产文化”；B 把责任推给学生，与作者立场相反；C 把“影响”说成“有助于丰富”，方向错误。

sections.title: Text 3　办公室话术的温度
sections.dir: Read the following four texts. Answer the questions below each text by choosing A, B, C or D. Mark your answers on the ANSWER SHEET. (40 points)
sections.note: 主线：企业语言越来越“感性、团队化、讲意义”。35 题要抓住 irony——人人取笑却人人照用。

paras.en: Even in traditional offices, "the lingua franca of corporate America has gotten much more emotional and much more right-brained than it was 20 years ago," said Harvard Business School professor Nancy Koehn. She started spinning off examples. "If you and I parachuted back to Fortune 500 companies in 1990, we would see much less frequent use of terms like journey, mission, passion. There were goals, there were strategies, there were objectives, but we didn't talk about energy; we didn't talk about passion."
paras.zh: 哈佛商学院教授南希·科恩说：“即便在传统办公室里，美国企业界的通用语也比 20 年前感性得多、右脑化得多了。”她随即举出一串例子。“如果你我空降回 1990 年的《财富》500 强企业，我们会发现 journey、mission、passion 这类词的使用频率低得多。那时有目标、有战略、有目的，但我们不谈能量，也不谈激情。”

paras.en: Koehn pointed out that this new era of corporate vocabulary is very "team"-oriented - and not by coincidence. "Let's not forget sports - in male-dominated corporate America, it's still a big deal. It's not explicitly conscious; it's the idea that I'm a coach, and you're my team, and we're in this together. There are lots and lots of CEOs in very different companies, but most think of themselves as coaches and this is their team and they want to win."
paras.zh: 科恩指出，新时代的企业词汇非常“团队”导向——这并非巧合。“别忘了体育——在男性主导的美国企业界，体育仍是件大事。这并不是明确意识到的，而是一种观念：我是教练，你是我的队伍，我们同舟共济。形形色色的公司里有许许多多 CEO，但多数人把自己看作教练，这是他们的队伍，他们想赢。”

paras.en: These terms are also intended to infuse work with meaning — and, as Rakesh Khurana, another professor, points out, increase allegiance to the firm. "You have the importation of terminology that historically used to be associated with non-profit organizations and religious organizations: terms like vision, values, passion, and purpose," said Khurana.
paras.zh: 这些词还意在为工作注入意义——并且，正如另一位教授拉凯什·库拉纳所指出的，增强对公司的忠诚。“你引入了那些历史上原本与非营利组织和宗教组织相连的术语：愿景、价值观、激情、使命，”库拉纳说。

paras.en: This new focus on personal fulfillment can help keep employees motivated amid increasingly loud debates over work-life balance. The "mommy wars" of the 1990s are still going on today, prompting arguments about why women still can't have it all and books like Sheryl Sandberg's Lean In, whose title has become a buzzword in its own right. Terms like unplug, offline, lifehack, bandwidth, and capacity are all about setting boundaries between the office and the home. But if your work is your "passion," you'll be more likely to devote yourself to it, even if that means going home for dinner and then working long after the kids are in bed.
paras.zh: 这种对个人成就感的新关注，能在工作与生活平衡的争论日益喧闹之际让员工保持干劲。20 世纪 90 年代的“妈妈大战”至今仍在继续，引发了关于女性为何仍无法兼顾一切的争论，也催生了谢丽尔·桑德伯格《向前一步》这类书，其书名本身已成流行语。unplug、offline、lifehack、bandwidth、capacity 这类词，说的都是在办公室与家之间划界。但如果你的工作就是你的“激情”，你会更愿意投入其中——哪怕这意味着回家吃完晚饭、等孩子睡下后再工作很久。

paras.en: But this seems to be the irony of office speak: Everyone makes fun of it, but managers love it, companies depend on it, and regular people willingly absorb it. As a linguist once said, "You can get people to think it's nonsense at the same time that you buy into it." In a workplace that's fundamentally indifferent to your life and its meaning, office speak can help you figure out how you relate to your work — and how your work defines who you are.
paras.zh: 但这似乎正是办公室话术的讽刺之处：人人都拿它打趣，可管理者喜欢它，公司依赖它，普通人也心甘情愿地接受它。正如一位语言学家所说：“你可以让人一边觉得它是废话，一边又照单全收。”在一个对你的生活及其意义根本漠不关心的职场里，办公室话术倒能帮你弄清自己与工作的关系——以及工作如何定义你是谁。

items.stem: According to Nancy Koehn, office language has become
items.exp: 定位首段①句 the lingua franca of corporate America has gotten much more emotional and much more right-brained：科恩直接说企业通用语“更感性、更右脑化”，D 为原词复现。A、C 与此方向相反；B 借 energy 一词设套，但文中说的是“那时不谈 energy”，并非语言本身失去活力。

items.stem: "Team"-oriented corporate vocabulary is closely related to
items.exp: 定位第二段②句 Let's not forget sports - in male-dominated corporate America, it's still a big deal，随后用 coach、team、win 一整套体育比喻解释团队导向，故 A。B 的 male-dominated 只是背景限定，本段落在体育而非性别；C 无据；D 把“CEO 像教练一样思考”错解成“运动型高管”。

items.stem: Khurana believes that the importation of terminology aims to
items.exp: 定位第三段①句 These terms are also intended to ... increase allegiance to the firm：allegiance 即“忠诚”，D 是其同义替换。A 把 historically used to be associated 误读为“复兴历史词汇”；B company image、C cooperation 都不是这种“术语引入”的目的。

items.stem: It can be inferred that Lean In
items.exp: 定位第四段②句 books like Sheryl Sandberg's Lean In：该书出现在“女性为何仍无法兼顾一切”的争论中，为职场女性发声，故 A。C 把论证顺序颠倒——“妈妈大战”引发争论、争论催生书籍，书不是争论的起因；B、D 谈热爱工作与激励员工，与该书主题不符。

items.stem: Which of the following statements is true about office speak?
opts: Linguists believe it to be nonsense.
Regular people mock it but accept it.
Companies find it to be fundamental.
Managers admire it but avoid it.
items.exp: 定位末段①句 Everyone makes fun of it, but managers love it, companies depend on it, and regular people willingly absorb it：普通人一边取笑一边接受，故 B。A 把语言学家转述的那句“你可以让人一边觉得它是废话一边接受”安到语言学家自己头上；C 是对 fundamentally indifferent 的误用；D 与 managers love it 直接相反。

sections.title: Text 4　被忽视的自愿兼职
sections.dir: Read the following four texts. Answer the questions below each text by choosing A, B, C or D. Mark your answers on the ANSWER SHEET. (40 points)
sections.note: 主线：就业数据背后，“自愿兼职”大增，与奥巴马医改解绑医保有关。38 题 D 与“仍远高于衰退前”直接冲突。

paras.en: Many people talked of the 288,000 new jobs the Labor Department reported for June, along with the drop in the unemployment rate to 6.1 percent, as good news. And they were right. For now it appears the economy is creating jobs at a decent pace. We still have a long way to go to get back to full employment, but at least we are now finally moving forward at a faster pace.
paras.zh: 劳工部报告 6 月新增 28.8 万个岗位，失业率降至 6.1%，许多人把这两件事当作好消息来谈。他们说得没错。目前看，经济正以尚可的速度创造就业。要回到充分就业，我们还有很长的路要走，但至少我们现在终于以更快的速度向前迈进了。

paras.en: However, there is another important part of the jobs picture that was largely overlooked. There was a big jump in the number of people who report voluntarily working part-time. This figure is now 830,000 ( 4.4 percent ) above its year ago level.
paras.zh: 然而，就业图景中还有另一个重要部分被大大忽视了：自称“自愿”从事兼职的人数大幅跃升。这一数字目前比一年前高出 83 万（4.4%）。

paras.en: Before explaining the connection to the Obamacare, it is worth making an important distinction. Many people who work part-time jobs actually want full-time jobs. They take part-time work because this is all they can get. An increase in involuntary part-time work is evidence of weakness in the labor market and it means that many people will be having a very hard time making ends meet.
paras.zh: 在解释这与奥巴马医改的关联之前，有必要先作一个重要区分。许多做兼职的人其实想要全职工作，他们接受兼职只是因为只能找到这样的工作。非自愿兼职的增加是劳动力市场疲弱的证据，也意味着许多人将很难维持生计。

paras.en: There was an increase in involuntary part-time in June, but the general direction has been down. Involuntary part-time employment is still far higher than before the recession, but it is down by 640,000 (7.9 percent) from its year ago level.
paras.zh: 6 月非自愿兼职有所增加，但总体趋势是下降的。非自愿兼职就业仍远高于衰退前的水平，不过已比一年前减少了 64 万（7.9%）。

paras.en: We know the difference between voluntary and involuntary part-time employment because people tell us. The survey used by the Labor Department asks people if they worked less than 35 hours in the reference week. If the answer is "yes," they are classified as working part-time. The survey then asks whether they worked less than 35 hours in that week because they wanted to work less than full time or because they had no choice. They are only classified as voluntary part-time workers if they tell the survey taker they chose to work less than 35 hours a week.
paras.zh: 我们之所以能区分自愿与非自愿兼职，是因为人们自己告诉了我们。劳工部采用的调查会问受访者在参照周内的工作时间是否少于 35 小时。如果回答“是”，他们就被归为兼职工作者。调查随后会问，那一周工作少于 35 小时，是因为想干得比全职少，还是因为别无选择。只有当他们告诉调查员是自己选择每周工作少于 35 小时时，才会被归为自愿兼职者。

paras.en: The issue of voluntary part-time relates to Obamacare because one of the main purposes was to allow people to get insurance outside of employment. For many people, especially those with serious health conditions or family members with serious health conditions, before Obamacare the only way to get insurance was through a job that provided health insurance.
paras.zh: 自愿兼职这一问题与奥巴马医改相关，因为医改的主要目的之一就是让人们能在就业之外获得保险。对许多人来说，尤其是那些本人或家人患有严重疾病的人，在医改之前，获得保险的唯一途径就是找一份提供医疗保险的工作。

paras.en: However, Obamacare has allowed more than 12 million people to either get insurance through Medicaid or the exchanges. These are people who may previously have felt the need to get a full-time job that provided insurance in order to cover themselves and their families. With Obamacare there is no longer a link between employment and insurance.
paras.zh: 然而，奥巴马医改已让超过 1200 万人得以通过医疗补助计划或保险交易所获得保险。这些人此前可能觉得必须找一份提供保险的全职工作，才能为自己和家人提供保障。有了医改，就业与保险之间不再挂钩。

items.stem: Which part of the jobs picture was neglected?
opts: The prospect of a thriving job market.
The increase of voluntary part-time jobs.
items.exp: 定位第二段：段首 there is another important part of the jobs picture that was largely overlooked，紧接着点明 There was a big jump in the number of people who report voluntarily working part-time，被忽视的正是自愿兼职人数大增，故 B。A、D 是首段已被广泛谈论的好消息；C 只是“仍有距离”的目标，不是被忽视的细节。

items.stem: Many people work part-time because they
opts: prefer part-time jobs to full-time jobs
feel that is enough to make ends meet
cannot get their hands on full-time jobs
haven' t seen the weakness of the market
items.exp: 定位第三段②③句 Many people who work part-time jobs actually want full-time jobs. They take part-time work because this is all they can get：做兼职是因为只能找到这样的工作，即拿不到全职，故 C。A 与 actually want full-time jobs 相反；B 与 making ends meet 很困难相反；D 与“市场疲弱”的论断不符。

items.stem: Involuntary part-time employment in the US
opts: shows a general tendency of decline
is harder to acquire than one year ago
satisfies the real need of the jobless
is lower than before the recession
items.exp: 定位第四段①句 but the general direction has been down：非自愿兼职总体趋于下降，故 A。D 与②句 still far higher than before the recession 直接冲突，是最强干扰；B 把“人数下降”说成“更难获得兼职”；C 与 involuntary（非自愿）的性质矛盾。

items.stem: It can be learned that with Obamacare,
opts: it is no longer easy for part-timers to get insurance
full-time employment is still essential for insurance
it is still challenging to get insurance for family members
employment is no longer a precondition to get insurance
items.exp: 定位末段末句 With Obamacare there is no longer a link between employment and insurance，且⑥段说医改目的是 allow people to get insurance outside of employment：就业不再是获得保险的前提，故 D。A 把“更容易”说反；B 与 no longer a link 相反；C 与 1200 多万人已获保险的事实不符。

items.stem: The text mainly discusses
items.exp: 全文由新增就业数据引出，主体是自愿与非自愿兼职的结构变化及其与医保的关系，落点都在美国就业状况，故 A。B 只是第五段的分类方法，属局部；C、D 仅是解释兼职变化的一个原因，且 Obamacare 在文中是“起了解绑作用”，并非“麻烦”，均不足以概括全文。

sections.title: Section II Part B　小标题匹配（七选五）
sections.dir: Read the following text and answer the questions by choosing the most suitable subheading from the list A-G for each of the numbered paragraphs (41-45). There are two extra subheadings which you do not need to use. Mark your answers on the ANSWER SHEET. (10 points)
sections.note: 五个空格各有一段，小标题多是段首句的同义改写。D 与 F 都谈“恐惧”，41 段落在“恐惧不真实”。
subs: Most of your fears are unreal
Don't fear responsibility for your life
There are many things to be grateful for
sections.intro:
Some Old Truths to Help You Overcome Tough Times

Unfortunately, life is not a bed of roses. We are going through life facing sad experiences. Moreover, we are grieving various kinds of loss: a friendship, a romantic relationship or a house. Hard times may hold you down at what usually seems like the most inopportune time, but you should remember that they won't last forever.

When our time of mourning is over, we press forward, stronger with a greater understanding and respect for life. Furthermore, these losses make us mature and eventually move us toward future opportunities for growth and happiness. I want to share these old truths I've learned along the way.

blocks.en: Fear is both useful and harmful. This normal human reaction is used to protect us by signaling danger and preparing us to deal with it. Unfortunately, people create inner barriers with a help of exaggerating fears. My favorite actor Will Smith once said, "Fear is not real. It is a product of thoughts you create. Do not misunderstand me. Danger is very real. But fear is a choice." I do completely agree that fears are just the product of our luxuriant imagination.
blocks.zh: 恐惧既是有用的，也是有害的。这种正常的人类反应通过发出危险信号、让我们做好准备来保护我们。不幸的是，人们借着夸大恐惧，给自己筑起了内心的壁垒。我最喜欢的演员威尔·史密斯曾说：“恐惧并不真实，它是你自己想法的产物。别误解我，危险是真实存在的，但恐惧是一种选择。”我完全同意：恐惧不过是我们过度丰富的想象力的产物。
blocks.exp: 定位段末 I do completely agree that fears are just the product of our luxuriant imagination，再加上威尔·史密斯那句 Fear is not real / Danger is very real：本段反复论证“恐惧多半是想出来的”，故 D。F 也带 fear 一词，但说的是“别怕为人生负责”，本段谈的是恐惧本身不真实，责任只字未提，是最强干扰。

blocks.en: If you are surrounded by problems and cannot stop thinking about the past, try to focus on the present moment. Many of us are weighed down by the past or anxious about the future. You may feel guilt over your past, but you are poisoning the present with the things and circumstances you cannot change. Value the present moment and remember how fortunate you are to be alive. Enjoy the beauty of the world around and keep the eyes open to see the possibilities before you. Happiness is not a point of future and not a moment from the past, but a mindset that can be designed into the present.
blocks.zh: 如果你被问题包围、止不住地想过去，那就试着专注于当下。我们中许多人被过去压得喘不过气，或对未来忧心忡忡。你可能为自己的过去感到内疚，但你正用那些无法改变的事与境况毒害当下。珍惜此刻，记住自己活着是多么幸运。欣赏周围世界的美，睁大眼睛看清眼前的可能性。幸福不是未来的某个点，也不是过去的某一刻，而是一种可以被设计进当下的心态。
blocks.exp: 定位首句 try to focus on the present moment 与末句 Happiness is ... a mindset that can be designed into the present：全段围绕“活在当下”，故 E。G 在 remember how fortunate you are 处似有影子，但“幸运”只是劝人珍惜当下的一个论据，落点仍是 present moment，不至于是主旨。

blocks.en: Sometimes it is easy to feel bad because you are going through tough times. You can be easily caught up by life problems that you forget to pause and appreciate the things you have. Only strong people prefer to smile and value their life instead of crying and complaining about something.
blocks.zh: 有时，因为正经历艰难，人很容易情绪低落。你容易被生活中的问题缠住，忘了停下来感激自己所拥有的东西。只有坚强的人才会选择微笑、珍视自己的生活，而不是哭诉和抱怨。
blocks.exp: 定位第二句 you forget to pause and appreciate the things you have：本段劝人别只盯着问题，要停下来感激已有的一切，故 G。E 的 present moment 已在上一段用过，本段没有“过去—当下—未来”的时间维度，是最近的一个干扰项。

blocks.en: No matter how isolated you might feel and how serious the situation is, you should always remember that you are not alone. Try to keep in mind that almost everyone respects and wants to help you if you are trying to make a good change in your life, especially your dearest and nearest people. You may have a circle of friends who provide constant good humor, help and companionship. If you have no friends or relatives, try to participate in several online communities, full of people who are always willing to share advice and encouragement.
blocks.zh: 无论你感到多么孤立、处境多么严峻，都应始终记住：你并不孤单。要记住，只要你在努力做出好的改变，几乎每个人都尊重你、愿意帮你，尤其是你最亲近的人。你或许有一圈朋友，能不断带来欢笑、帮助与陪伴。如果你没有亲友，就试着加入几个网络社群，那里满是愿意分享建议和鼓励的人。
blocks.exp: 定位首句 you should always remember that you are not alone，与 A 逐词重合；后文“亲友、网友都愿意帮你”正是对这个判断的支撑。F 的 Don't fear 只是劝慰语气，本段核心是“有人与你同在”，与“责任”无关。

blocks.en: Today many people find it difficult to trust their own opinion and seek balance by gaining objectivity from external sources. This way you devalue your opinion and show that you are incapable of managing your own life. When you are struggling to achieve something important you should believe in yourself and be sure that your decision is the best. You live in your skin, think your own thoughts, have your own values and make your own choices.
blocks.zh: 如今许多人难以相信自己的判断，转而从外部来源获取客观性以求平衡。这样做其实是在贬低自己的意见，表明你无力经营自己的生活。当你为某件重要的事奋力拼搏时，你应当相信自己，确信自己的决定是最好的。你活在自己的身体里，想自己的念头，有自己的价值观，做自己的选择。
blocks.exp: 定位末句 You live in your skin, think your own thoughts, have your own values and make your own choices：主张信自己、走自己的路，与 C 的 Pave your own unique path 对应。B 的 Experience helps you grow 与本段“别向外求客观”无关，只是“成长”这一主题词的泛化干扰。

sections.title: Section III　翻译
sections.dir: Translate the following text into Chinese. Write your translation on the ANSWER SHEET. (15 points)
sections.note: 难点：well-travelled road effect 译“熟路效应”；allocate 是“分配”不是“集中”。

paras.en: Think about driving a route that's very familiar. It could be your commute to work, a trip into town or the way home. Whichever it is, you know every twist and turn like the back of your hand. On these sorts of trips it's easy to lose concentration on the driving and pay little attention to the passing scenery. The consequence is that you perceive that the trip has taken less time than it actually has.
paras.zh: 想一想开车走一条非常熟悉的路线的情形。它可能是你上班的通勤路，可能是进城的路，也可能是回家的路。无论是哪一种，你对每一个转弯都了如指掌。在这样的行程中，人很容易在驾驶上走神，很少留意沿途的景色。其结果是，你会觉得这段路花的时间比实际要短。

paras.en:
This is the well-travelled road effect: People tend to underestimate the time it takes to travel a familiar route.

The effect is caused by the way we allocate our attention. When we travel down a well-known route, because we don't have to concentrate much, time seems to flow more quickly. And afterwards, when we come to think back on it, we can't remember the journey well because we didn't pay much attention to it. So we assume it was shorter.
paras.zh:
这就是“熟路效应”：人们往往会低估走一条熟悉路线所花的时间。

这种效应源于我们分配注意力的方式。当我们行驶在熟悉的路上时，由于不必高度集中注意力，时间似乎过得更快。而在事后回想时，我们又记不清这段旅程，因为当时并没怎么留意它。于是我们便认为它更短。

words: like the back of your hand

sections.title: Section IV Part A　应用文（通知·招募夏令营志愿者）
sections.dir: Suppose your university is going to host a summer camp for high school students. Write a notice to 1) briefly introduce the camp activities, and 2) call for volunteers. You should write about 100 words on the ANSWER SHEET. Do not use your name or the name of your university. Do not write your address. (10 points)
sections.note: 文体是通知，不是书信：Notice 居中，正文讲活动再招志愿者，末尾署名单位，不写个人姓名与校名。
sections.sample:
Notice

A summer camp for high school students will be held on our campus from July 15 to July 22, and about 200 students from local high schools are expected to take part.

The camp offers a wide range of activities: morning lectures on science and culture, afternoon workshops in robotics and painting, and a sports day on the final afternoon. A campus tour and a farewell party will also be arranged.

We are now recruiting 30 volunteers. Helpers are needed to guide the groups, run the workshops and stay with the students during the week. Anyone interested should send an application to the Students' Union office before July 1.

The Students' Union
tips: 格式先立住：Notice 居中作标题，正文分段，末尾用单位署名（The Students' Union），不出现个人姓名与校名
两个要点都要落实：先用两三句把夏令营的时间、对象和具体活动说清楚，再写招募人数、职责和报名方式
活动要具体到“讲座、工作坊、运动会”这一层，只写 interesting activities 拿不到内容分；语气是招募，可用 We are now recruiting… Anyone interested should…

sections.title: Section IV Part B　图表作文
sections.dir: Write an essay based on the following chart. In your writing, you should 1) interpret the chart, and 2) give your comments. You should write about 150 words on the ANSWER SHEET. (15 points)
sections.note: 饼图：新年礼物 40%，聚会吃饭、交通、其他各 20%。三个 20% 要合并说“其余三项均分”，别逐项堆数字。
sections.sample:
The pie chart shows how residents of a Chinese city spent their money during the Spring Festival holiday. New Year gifts accounted for the largest share, 40 percent, while family dinners, transport and other items each took up 20 percent.

Two features stand out. First, gifts dominate the budget, which confirms that exchanging presents remains the core of Spring Festival etiquette. Second, the remaining three items are evenly distributed at one fifth each, suggesting that dining out and travelling home have become a routine part of the holiday rather than a luxury.

This pattern reflects both tradition and change. People are still willing to spend generously on gifts, yet the money paid for dinners and transport shows that a family reunion now often means travelling back home and eating in a restaurant. In my view, such spending is reasonable as long as it stays within people's means, for the festival is ultimately about reunion rather than extravagance.
tips: 第一段只读数：礼物 40%，其余三项各 20%，用 accounted for / took up 两个不同动词，避免句式重复
第二段做归纳：40% 说明“送礼仍是人情核心”，三个 20% 说明“聚餐与出行已成常规开销”，这一步是从数据到意义的转换
第三段评价要有一句两面：拉动消费、维系亲情是正面，攀比浪费是隐忧，最后落到“量力而行、重在团圆”
